thread:
zoe: Heads-up — noticed provisioner rejects ~15% of GPU launches in us-west1 around 02:00 UTC. Correlates with high ephemeral-cleaner CPU & nvme iops. Janitor backlog grew to 18k. Logs: scrubber loop invoked 4k/s, evict queue starved. Anyone else seeing this? :thinking:

rajiv: Yep. Saw deploy failures for big-batch jobs. Provisioning logs show `scratchpool.io_wait>1500ms` then `gpu-attach-timeout`.

eli: pinging infra-bot for metrics.

infra-bot: Janitor backlog metric spike: scratch-cleaner.deferred_count=17982, scrub_ops/s=4100, avg_nvme_iops=34000 (nvme-local-us-west1), gpu_attach_failures=23 in last 15m.

sophie: Is this the deep-clean job that started after the image-cached compaction? We rolled compaction -> continuous at 01:45.

rajiv: Yes — compaction + deep-scrub overlap. Deep-scrub is low-priority but concurrency explodes when many small-file GC passes run; that saturates NVMe and blocks attach paths.

max: Quick mitigation: can we pause deep-scrub in us-west1 for 1h? `janitorctl pause --selector=region=us-west1 --job=deep-scrub`

zoe: I'd prefer targeted rate-limit instead of full pause. Pausing increases risk of tombstone buildup. Proposal: throttle scrub concurrency from 64 -> 12 and bump janitor reclaim-threshold to 0.15 so reclaim is less aggressive during high IO.

eli: Command to change config shown below:
```
janitorctl update-config --region us-west1 --concurrency-scrub=12 --reclaim-threshold=0.15
```

rajiv: Will that free enough IOPS? We need to avoid starving the NVMe scheduler and causing more attach timeouts.

sophie: Also can we shift heavy clean/compaction windows to off-peak: move scheduled heavy-clean to 05:00-08:00 UTC? That avoids overlap with customer batch window at 01:30-03:00 UTC.

zoe: OK. Quick plan:
- Reduce scrub concurrency to 12 now (rajiv)
- Shift compaction/paid-clean window to 05:00 UTC (sophie + max)
- Add temporary soft-quota on janitor CPU in us-west1 so it can't spike beyond 30% (eli)
- Monitor GPU attach failures & nvme iops for 1h

rajiv: Doing concurrency change now.

infra-bot: Applying config change... success. concurrency_scrub: 64 -> 12. reclaim_threshold: 0.20 -> 0.15. (change-id: cfg-8932)

zoe: Observed initial drop in nvme iops from ~34k -> ~12k in 3m. GPU attach failures down to 2 in last 10m. Looks promising. :thumbsup: 

max: I'll open a short incident note if this recurs. Long-term we should implement preemptible janitor that yields to attach-critical flows and per-pool IOPS budgets.

sophie: Agree. Add to backlog: preemptible-cleaner + per-pool IOPS quotas + scheduled compaction windows.

eli: Filing ticket INFRA-4403: "Janitor preemption + per-pool IOPS quotas". Attaching metric links and graphs.

zoe: Thanks team. Keep eyes on us-west1 for next 2 hours. If any regression, @here.
